html:
On the 1492 and 1500 maps, Rajastan is the land of the Rajput kingdoms in the dry north west of India, today's Rajasthan.

Around 1500 it was a set of strong clan kingdoms, each with hill forts and its own ruling house:

  • Mewar, under Rana Raimal and from 1508 Rana Sanga, with its fortress at Chittor;
  • Marwar, whose capital Jodhpur Rao Jodha founded in 1459;
  • Bikaner, founded by his son Rao Bika in 1488;
  • Amber of the Kachwahas, and Jaisalmer in the desert.

They fought each other and the Muslim sultans of Delhi, Gujarat and Malwa. With the Delhi Sultanate weak, Rana Sanga led a league of Rajput kings that was the strongest power in the north. In 1527 he met Babur at the Battle of Khanwa and lost, which opened the way for Mughal rule. See Rajputana for the next century.
sum: On the 1492 and 1500 maps, Rajastan is the land of the Rajput kingdoms in the dry north west of India, today's Rajasthan.
